key_insight: UnDA transfers useful structural knowledge between medical imaging modalities without paired data by aligning semantically structured class tokens and down-weighting uncertain predictions.
clinical_relevance: This could help build better segmentation models when matched multimodal clinical datasets are unavailable, improving robustness across heterogeneous imaging sources.
method: Backbone-agnostic Alignment Module uses attention-based pooling to extract class tokens.
Uncertainty-Weighted Optimal Transport (UCT-OT) suppresses noisy supervision by weighting alignment with prediction confidence.
Per-class ProtoNCE maintains prototype memories to preserve global class separability across unpaired batches.
evidence_signal: On representative segmentation tasks under strictly unpaired settings, the method consistently improved accuracy and boundary precision in the target modality.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well prediction confidence reflects true uncertainty, and the approach still requires careful tuning for different modality gaps.
paper_title: UnDA: Unpaired Domain Alignment for Cross-Modal Knowledge Transfer in Medical Imaging
